en: The Sūtra of the Prajñāpāramitā of Universal Radiance Spoken by the Buddha,
translated by the Tripitaka Master Śīladharma, Imperially Appointed Court Dispersing Grandee and Acting Minister of State Ceremonial,
Dharma-Transmitting Master, Subject Śīladharma, by Imperial Decree.

Thus have I heard: At one time, the Bhagavān attained the vajra-samādhi-wisdom of all Tathāgatas; he attained the various and fully perfected supreme jewel crowns of all Tathāgatas; he attained the vajra-wisdom corresponding to the great sovereignty of all Tathāgatas; he received the empowerment of the three realms and the wisdom-seals of all Tathāgatas; and he fulfilled the desired vows of all sentient beings to their full extent. Through various transformations, the great luminosity of equalizing wisdom, this Great Vairocana—who eternally abides as the vajra-body, speech, and mind of all Tathāgatas equal throughout the three times—extolled all Tathāgatas.

At that time, the World-Honored One was dwelling in the palace of the Paranirmita-vaśavartin Heaven within the Desire Realm; this palace was fully adorned with all manner of magnificent ornaments, including various wonderful-colored great maṇi jewels, various pearl necklaces, various banners, pennants, and precious canopies, with various jeweled bells suspended from them.
There was an assembly of bodhisattva-mahāsattvas, whose names were:

Vajrapāṇi Bodhisattva, Avalokiteśvara Bodhisattva, Ākāśagarbha Bodhisattva, Vajramuṣṭi Bodhisattva, Samānacittotpādadharmacakrapravartana Bodhisattva, Gaganagañja Bodhisattva, Sarvamārapramardin Bodhisattva, and Mañjuśrī Bodhisattva.
To this assembly of sixty-eight koṭis of bodhisattva-mahāsattvas, who were respectfully surrounding him, he preached the Dharma—good in the beginning, good in the middle, and good in the end;
profound in meaning and exquisite in expression; pure, unadulterated, complete, and immaculate. He proclaimed all the dharmas of purification for bodhisattvas:
"If sentient beings are purified regarding desire, it is because they are bodhisattvas."
The purity of the fetter of craving is because of this bodhisattva;
the purity of all conditioned phenomena is because of this bodhisattva;
the purity of seeing the nature is because of this bodhisattva.
Because love and delight are pure, they are Bodhisattvas;
because craving is pure, they are Bodhisattvas;
because hatred is pure, they are Bodhisattvas.
Delusion is pure because it is the Bodhisattva;
the storehouse is pure because it is the Bodhisattva;
and letters are pure because they are the Bodhisattva.
Purity of intention, because they are bodhisattvas;
purity of observation, because they are bodhisattvas;
purity of body, because they are bodhisattvas.
Speech is pure because it is the Bodhisattva;
mind is pure because it is the Bodhisattva;
form is pure because it is the Bodhisattva.
Sound is pure because it is the Bodhisattva;
fragrance is pure because it is the Bodhisattva;
taste is pure because it is the Bodhisattva.
Contact is pure because it is a bodhisattva.
What do you think?
All phenomena are empty of intrinsic nature and pure by intrinsic nature; likewise, the perfection of wisdom is also empty of intrinsic nature and pure by intrinsic nature.
The Buddha addressed the Bodhisattva Vajrapāṇi:
“Within this Prajñāpāramitā, the Dharma-gate of universal purity, there is the secret syllable HŪṂ, which encompasses all phenomena.”
The Buddha told Vajrapāṇi Bodhisattva:

“Regarding this Prajñāpāramitā, the Dharma-gate of universal purity, if anyone listens to, receives, reads, or recites it, that person shall immediately enter the bodhimanda. All karmic obstructions, retributive obstructions, and afflictive obstructions, as well as the hells, evil destinies, and all hindrances and entanglements, shall never arise; all suffering and distress shall be utterly extinguished.”

If there should be another person who, day by day, upholds, recites, and contemplates with single-minded focus, that person will, in this very life, attain the Vajra Samādhi of the Equality of All Dharmas; they will obtain all sovereign delights and peace, enter the stage of a Bodhisattva, and swiftly realize the fruit of Buddhahood. For this reason, they are named the Vajradhara Buddha.
"All the dharmas and practices thus described are subsumed within the gateway of the meaning of the secret syllable HŪṂ.
At that time, the Tathāgata Samantaprabhāsa addressed the Bodhisattva Vajrapāṇi:
"This Prajñāpāramitā Sūtra expounds the quiescent dharma-bodhi of all Tathāgatas."
That is to say:
the vajra-equality bodhi; the vajra-solidity-meaning-equality bodhi;
The awakening that is firm in the single meaning of phenomena,
and the awakening that is the intrinsic purity of all phenomena—
these are all Great Awakening (mahābodhi), which can eliminate all false conceptualizations and the like.

If there are those who hear, receive, read, recite, revere, and make offerings to it, all their karmic obstructions will be eliminated; they shall even reach the seat of enlightenment and swiftly realize *anuttara-samyak-saṃbodhi*.
"All such practices of the dharmas as have been described are subsumed within the gateway of the meaning of the secret syllable Aṃ.
At that time, Śākyamuni Tathāgata, in order to subdue all evils, spoke the *Sarvadharma-samatā-parama-prajñāpāramitā Sūtra*: "The conceptual proliferation of desire should be seen as desire itself;
[the conceptual proliferation of hatred should be seen as hatred itself; the conceptual proliferation of delusion should be seen as delusion itself]."
One should see the conceptual proliferation of delusion as delusion;
one should see the conceptual proliferation of all phenomena as all phenomena.
The Prajñāpāramitā should be understood in this way.
"All these dharmas and practices as thus explained are subsumed within the gateway of the secret syllable *HŪṂ*.
The Buddha addressed the Bodhisattva Vajrapāṇi:

"If there is anyone who hears, receives, upholds, recites, and contemplates this Prajñāpāramitā, even if that person were to slaughter all sentient beings throughout the three realms, the immeasurable and boundless sins they have committed would be swiftly eliminated by the power of this merit from recitation and upholding, and they shall realize *anuttara-samyak-saṃbodhi*."
"All such dharmas and practices as have been explained are subsumed within the gateway of the meaning of the secret syllable *HŪṂ*.
At that time, the Tathāgata of Innate Purity further spoke the *Sarvadharma-saṃgraha-avalokiteśvara-jñāna-mudrā-prajñāpāramitā-sūtra*:

"Because all worldly greed is pure, all hatred is pure, all defilements are pure, all transgressions are pure, all sentient beings are pure, all dharmas are pure, all wisdom is pure, and the *prajñāpāramitā* is pure."
The Buddha addressed the Bodhisattva Vajrapāṇi:

“If there is anyone who hears, receives, upholds, recites, and contemplates this Prajñāpāramitā, that person, though situated in the mire of all sensual desires, cannot be defiled by the afflictions of desire, just as a red lotus is not stained by the mud. In this way, such a person shall before long attain Anuttara-samyak-saṃbodhi.”
At that time, the Tathāgata, Lord of All Three Realms, spoke the *Sarvatathāgatābhiṣekajñānagarbha-prajñāpāramitā-sūtra*:
"If one bestows consecration, one shall obtain the body of a sovereign king over all within the three realms;
if one performs beneficial conduct, one shall obtain the complete fulfillment of all desired wishes."
If one practices the gift of Dharma, one will swiftly realize all dharmas of equality;
if one practices the gift of material wealth, one will experience all happiness of body, speech, and mind.
All such dharmic practices as described herein are subsumed within the gateway of the secret syllable *tāḷan*.
At that time, the Tathāgata Sarvajñatāmudrāpratilabdhanityasarvaguhyadhara spoke the *Sarvatathāgatavajrajñānamudrāsthitaprajñāpāramitāsūtra*:
"If one receives the body-seal (*kāyamudrā*) of all Tathāgatas, one immediately accomplishes all Tathāgatas;
if one receives the speech-seal (*vāṅmudrā*), one immediately accomplishes all Dharma-gates."
If one receives the Mind Seal, one immediately accomplishes all samādhis;
if one receives the Vajra Seal, one immediately accomplishes the supreme vajra actions of body, speech, and mind of all Tathāgatas.
The Buddha addressed the Bodhisattva Vajrapāṇi:

“If there be anyone who hears, receives, upholds, recites, and contemplates this sutra, that person shall swiftly attain the fulfillment of wealth and honor, and swiftly achieve the secrets of the vajra body, speech, and mind; before long, they shall realize the supreme *anuttara-samyak-saṃbodhi*.”
"All the practices of all dharmas as thus explained are subsumed within the gateway of the secret meaning of the syllable *akṣara*.
At that time, the Tathāgata Sarvadharma-prapañca spoke the *Prajñāpāramitā-sūtra of the Turning Wheel Syllable*:

"Because all dharmas lack intrinsic nature, they are signless; because all dharmas are signless, they are unconditioned; because they are unconditioned, they are wishless; because they are wishless, all dharmas are primordially pure, and the *prajñāpāramitā* is pure."
"All the practices of all dharmas thus described are subsumed within the gateway of the meaning of the secret syllable *Aṃ*.
At that time, all the Tathāgatas of the Inner Wheel spoke the *Mahācakra-prajñāpāramitā-sūtra*:
"By entering into the equality of the vajra, one also enters the wheel of all Tathāgatas."
If one enters into equality with the vajra of benefit, one also gains entry into the wheel of all great bodhisattvas;
if one enters into equality with the Dharma, one also gains entry into the wheel of all dharmas;
and if one enters into the equality of all things, one also gains entry into all wheels.
"All such practices of the dharmas as have been explained are subsumed within the gateway of the secret syllable *laṃ*.
At that time, the Tathāgata Universal Arising of the Vast Ritual of All Offerings spoke the *Prajñāpāramitā Sūtra of the Supreme Offering of All Tathāgatas*:
"One should generate the bodhicitta and extensively extend offerings to all Tathāgatas;..."
To deliver all sentient beings, causing them to receive the sublime Dharma of all Tathāgatas; to transcribe, honor, uphold, recite, and chant it;
and furthermore, to obtain the vast offerings of all Tathāgatas.
"All such dharmas and practices as have been described are subsumed within the gateway of the secret meaning of the syllable *Oṃ*.
At that time, the Tathāgatas who Subdue All with Equanimity proclaimed the *Vajrapāṇi Sarvasattvavinaya-samyagjñānagarbha-prajñāpāramitā Sūtra*.
It is said:
"Because all sentient beings are equal, anger is also equal;
because all sentient beings are to be tamed, anger is also to be tamed."
Because all phenomena are equal, hatred is also equal;
because all sentient beings are equal, the vajra is also equal.
What do you think?
For the sake of awakening, one thus disciplines all sentient beings.
All these aforementioned practices of the Dharma are subsumed within the gateway of the meaning of the secret syllable *haṃ*.
At that time, the Tathāgata Abiding in the Equality of All Dharmas spoke the *Sarvadharma-samatā-paramārtha-prajñāpāramitā-sūtra*, saying:
"Because all things are equal, the *prajñāpāramitā* is also equal."
Because it benefits all, the Prajñāpāramitā is also beneficial;
because it is all dharmas, the Prajñāpāramitā is also a dharma;
because it is all karma, the Prajñāpāramitā is also karma.
"All the practices of all dharmas as thus explained are subsumed within the gateway of the secret syllable *hṛdaya*.
At that time, the Tathāgata Lokanātha spoke the *Sarvasattva-prajñāpāramitā-vyūha-sūtra*:
"The Tathāgatagarbha of all sentient beings is the treasury of the Great Bodhisattva Samantabhadra, because it is the self-nature of all things."
He is the treasury of the vajra, because he is consecrated by the vajra;
he is the treasury of the Dharma, because he transforms all speech;
he is the treasury of karma, because he performs all skillful deeds.
"All the practices of all dharmas thus explained are subsumed within the gateway of the secret syllable *hṛdaya*.
At that time, the Tathāgata Anantaparyanta-niṣṭha, abiding in the dharma of boundless ultimateity, spoke the *Sarvadharma-samatā-niṣṭha-vajra-prajñāpāramitā-sūtra*:
"Because the *prajñāpāramitā* is boundless, all Tathāgatas are also boundless; because the *prajñāpāramitā* is infinite, all Tathāgatas are also infinite."
Because all Tathāgatas are boundless, the Prajñāpāramitā is also boundless;
even unto the point that because the Prajñāpāramitā is of one suchness, all dharmas are of one suchness;
and because the Prajñāpāramitā is ultimate, all dharmas are also ultimate.
The Buddha addressed the Bodhisattva Vajrapāṇi:

"If there is anyone who hears, receives, upholds, recites, and reflects upon this Prajñāpāramitā, that person shall enter the stage of the ultimately pure bodhisattva practice; all veils and obscurations will never arise again, and they shall be named a Vajradhara Tathāgata."
"All such dharmas and practices as have been explained are subsumed within the gateway of the secret *vyañjana* (syllable) *Vī*.

At that time, the Tathāgata Mahāvairocana, having attained the secret dharma of all Tathāgatas and awakened to all dharmas of conceptual proliferation (*prapañca*), spoke this *Mahāsukha-Amoghavajra-Samādhi-Samatā-Prajñāpāramitā Sūtra*:

'The supreme gateway of Dharma is originally devoid of entities; it has no superior, middle, or inferior. If one can accomplish the bliss of the bodhi-dharma of all Tathāgatas, subdue Māras and enemies, attain mastery over the three realms, and even rescue and deliver all sentient beings, enabling them to obtain the most supreme benefit and joy, this is what is called a Great Earth Bodhisattva.'"
All these aforementioned practices of the Dharma are subsumed within the gateway of the secret meaning of the syllable *sraḥ*.
"Furthermore, Vajrapāṇi Bodhisattva!
Those great bodhisattvas, even while remaining within saṃsāra, perform all manner of beneficial deeds to deliver all sentient beings."

Abiding in the wisdom of skillful means, all undertakings are rendered completely pure; the afflictions of greed and desire cannot invade them, just as a lotus in water is not defiled by the mud. They dwell in sovereign peace and bliss, firm and non-retrogressive.
All these aforementioned practices of the dharmas are subsumed within the gateway of the meaning of the secret syllable *Ha*.
Furthermore, Vajrapāṇi Bodhisattva!

If a person correctly contemplates this Prajñāpāramitā Sūtra, reciting it daily, or even listening to it with sympathetic joy, that person shall obtain all happiness and further be able to accomplish the great bliss of the non-empty Vajra-samādhi.
"All such practices of the dharmas as have been explained are subsumed within the gateway of the meaning of the secret syllable HŪṂ.
At that time, the World-Honored One, the Tathāgata Samantaprabha, addressed the Great Lord of Secrets, Vajrapāṇi, saying:
"I shall now further explain twenty-five kinds of secret dharma-gateways of the Prajñāpāramitā."
Listen attentively now!
The mantra is: "Oṃ namo sarvabuddhabodhisattvebhyaḥ. Oṃ.
Āḥ Māṇicita-vajri | Oṃ surata-satve | Oṃ samantabhadra-caryā-vaipumani | Oṃ aniruddhe | Oṃ jati-vavrite |
Recite: Oṃ mahā-rāga-darime | Oṃ virya-kavacī | Oṃ sarva-gāmi | Oṃ vajra-dṛḍha-kavaca-citte.
HŪṂ | OṂ SARVA-TATHĀGATE | OṂ ŚAPAVĀ-ŚODHE | OṂ DHARMATĀ-JÑĀNA-VIŚODHA | OṂ KALMAṢA-VIŚODHANI HŪṂ | OṂ ||
niḥsvabhāvavajriṇi hūṃ phaṭ | oṃ kāmari | oṃ jaha vajri | oṃ sarvanāyike | oṃ hrīṃ | oṃ akā-
Āḥ Rāma-khe. Oṃ prajñāpāramitā-jñānāṅga hūṃ. Oṃ aṃ aṃ sarvatathāgatāgragarbha. Oṃ sarva...
tathāgatāvaviśodhani | oṃ sarvatathāgatajñānavajri āḥ | oṃ samayagrya sarvasattvān mocaya sarvapāpa...
*Ānīya-gate viya sarva-samaya-vajra hūṃ traṭ.* At that time,
having spoken this mantra, the World-Honored One addressed the Bodhisattva Vajrapāṇi:
"This seal-mantra can destroy all darkness of sin, bring about all auspiciousness, and is the supreme accomplishment of the vajra secrets of all Tathāgatas."
If a person attains this, upholds it, recites it, or hears it, they shall be named the Tathāgata Vajradhara-viśuddha.

If there are sentient beings who receive, uphold, read, recite, rejoice in, or hear this Prajñāpāramitā Sūtra, such persons have already planted various roots of goodness and established the foundations of all virtues under immeasurable Buddhas.
"Furthermore, Vajrapāṇi Bodhisattva!

If a person hears even a single four-line verse of this Prajñāpāramitā Sūtra, they will receive the respectful offerings of as many Tathāgatas as there are grains of sand in eighty thousand koṭis of nayutas of Ganges Rivers; how much more so for one who understands its meaning and expounds it for others."
Wherever that person holds this sutra, it shall be like a stupa or temple of the Buddha, and all devas, humans, asuras, and others will constantly come to pay homage.

If anyone circulates this sutra and reads or recites it from one to another, they will obtain the knowledge of past lives (*pūrvajātismṛti*) and be able to know the events of *koṭi* eons in the past; all māras and various evil calamities shall be unable to invade them, and the Four Great Heavenly Kings and all worthy sages will constantly provide protection.

When that person approaches the end of life, their mind will not be inverted; all Buddhas and great Bodhisattvas will come together to welcome them, and they will be reborn at will in the pure lands of the ten directions.
"Furthermore, Vajrapāṇi Bodhisattva!
This essential Dharma gate of the Prajñāpāramitā Sūtra accomplishes such supreme, excellent, and wondrous merit through the practice of the highest Dharma."

When the Buddha had finished preaching this sutra, Vajrapāṇi Bodhisattva Mahāsattva, as well as the devas, humans, asuras, gandharvas, and others, were all greatly rejoiced; they believed, accepted, and practiced it accordingly.
The Prajñāpāramitā Sūtra of Universal Illumination (Ling)
